candidates.reviewerRationale: Coverage value: Clear Seas Research gains operating context for remote-pilotage research, concrete anchorage analysis and historical financial context, replacing a generic marine-research description. Evidence: 9 sources include clearseas.org reports, audited statements, Transport Canada’s MELO contribution and MEOPAR’s SOC-I selection. The full progress report distinguishes modelling from later vessel validation. Mission/Public Need read: No new relationships are proposed; remote pilotage and risk assessment offer a bounded planning-research conversation. Unknowns: Current liquidity and an operational adaptive noise-control installation are not established; incorporation dates differ across records. Reviewer action: Inspect the operating context for Pilotage Technology Phase II and the disclosed financing summary, retain the stated research-stage limits, and review this private proposal before any separate publication.
reviewWarnings: The latest audited accounts found end March 31, 2025; they do not establish current liquidity or a 2026 funding runway.
MELO vessel validation and an operational adaptive noise-control installation are not established by the 2024 progress report; the later project page still describes research underway.
The annual report and audited notes use different incorporation or registration years; no founded_year or legal-name correction is proposed.
The inherited capability Mission Area relationship remains a needs_review derived mapping; this refresh does not assert a defence customer or validated defence performance.

candidates.reviewerRationale: Coverage value: Coastal Defence Systems gains ownership and operating context for the Lake Central acquisition and AEROVISTA manufacturing LOI, clarifying what changed in its industrial proposition. Evidence: 3 sources comprise the official portfolio and the two attributed Newsfile announcements from Coastal Defence Systems and Lake Central Air Services. Mission/Public Need read: No new relationships are proposed; intended manufacturing, training and lifecycle support make industrial integration a relevant conversation. Unknowns: An executed manufacturing licence, commissioned UAV production and a replacement headquarters address were not established. Reviewer action: Inspect ownership for the announced Lake Central acquisition and operating context for the AEROVISTA LOI; retain planned-stage wording and the stable Coastal identity pending any separately evidenced legal correction.
reviewWarnings: The buyer announces the acquisition and the Valkyrie trading identity; no legal-name replacement, successor redirect or archive is proposed for Coastal.
The July 6 AEROVISTA arrangement is an LOI. A definitive manufacturing licence or completed Canadian technology transfer was not recovered.
Planned Muskoka UAV production, the proposed public listing and company-stated platform specifications are not evidence of operational delivery, certification or awarded procurement.
The retained map point is the existing Halifax city centroid; the announcements refer to Windsor and the buyer’s Muskoka facility and do not establish a replacement Coastal headquarters address.
